title: Separation in a directed union of nested systems
statement: Let J be a nonempty directed partial order and V:J→Cᵒᵖ a diagram. A chain presentation consists of a partial order I, a nonempty directed partial order A of stages, an embedding e:J↪oI, a diagram U:I→Cᵒᵖ restricting to V, and increasing nonempty directed subsets I_a⊆I covering I and containing e(J). Then I is nonempty and directed. For any P:Cᵒᵖ→Type, if the canonical images [def-trf-point-system-refinement-map] of s,s′∈colim(V⋙P) are distinct in every colim(U|I_a⋙P), they are distinct in colim(U⋙P). Passing through any stage gives the canonical map to the union.

proof.text: Two indices of I belong to stages a,b; a common larger stage contains them and supplies an upper bound. Stage inclusions and original embeddings give the composition formula.

proof.text: Represent s,s′ at one original index j. Equality of their union images has a common-index witness by the filtered-colimit elementwise criterion. Choose a stage containing this witness; it already contains e(j). Restricting the witness arrows and their equality to this stage contradicts its separation hypothesis.
